To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the MDM-2 SNP309 G allele may have a protective effect against CRC in HNPCC, and that age of disease diagnosis is not associated with the MDM2 309 SNP and TP53 R72 SNP either as single SNPS or combined.

the MDM-2 SNP309 T/G does not appear to be a modifying factor in the development of colorectal cancer (CRC) in individuals with HNCC and that the MDM SNP309 T/G and the TP53 SNP R/P do not appear to influence the age of diagnosis of HNCC patients.

MDM2 SNP 309 and TP53 R72 are not associated with age of diagnosis in HNPCC and that there is no evidence that the TP53 R27P SNP is associated with the age of diagnosis of HNPCC patients in Australia and Poland.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of MDM2 and p53 polymorphisms in the expression of HNPCC, which is the second most common hereditary form of CRC.
the identification of genetic factors that influence disease expression in HNPCC and the development of a model to predict the age of disease onset.
the role of MDM2 and p53 gene polymorphisms in hereditary colorectal cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MDM 2 SNP309 and TP53 R72 P polymorphisms are not associated with the age of diagnosis of cancer in HNPCCC.
the MDM-2 SNP309 and TP53 SNP72 do not influence the age of onset of HNPCC.
the G allele of SNP309 in the MDM2 gene does not appear to have a significant impact on the age of diagnosis of HNPCC-associated CRC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MDM SNP 309 and TP53 R72 P do not influence the disease expression of HNPCC patients.
the MDM SNP309 and the TP53 R71P do not influence age at diagnosis of CRC in HNPCC.
there is a lack of evidence that the MDM 2 SNP309 and/or TP53 SNP R722P are involved in disease development in HNPPC patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MDM SNP309 G allele may be a modifier of disease expression in HNPCC, but this needs further investigation in other cohorts.
the MDM SNP309 T>G is not associated with disease expression and age at diagnosis in HNPCC.
the G allele of the MDM-2 SNP 309 might have a protecting effect on disease development and that age of CRC diagnosis is not associated with either the MDM2 or TP53 SNP alone or in combination.
